issues.legal_issue: Compensation for acquired land must reflect just and reasonable value when the land is materially comparable to nearby land for which a higher compensation has been determined.
material_facts: The acquired lands were in the same village as lands acquired for another project and lay directly across a road from them.
Some land in the same survey number was acquired for both projects.
The Supreme Court had previously determined higher compensation for the lands across the road, while the High Court had reduced compensation for the lands in these appeals to the Collector’s amount.
The notifications for the two acquisitions were issued at different times, but the Court found the lands similarly situated despite the time gap.
The Court considered the evidence on record and the sale instances relied on by the landowners.
issues.conclusion: The Court modified the High Court’s judgment and increased the compensation for the acquired lands to a just and reasonable level.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, compensation must be just and reasonable. The Court considered the similarity in location and the earlier determination in Arawali Power Company Private Limited (Civil Appeal No. 8757 of 2016 and connected appeals, decided 5 September 2017), while also considering the evidence and sale instances in the present case. Sections 4, 6 and 11 of the Act concerned the acquisition notifications, declaration and Collector’s award in this case.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and (comparable_location or shared_survey_land) and prior_comparable_award_higher and significant_compensation_difference

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.comparable_location: The acquired land is located comparably to other acquired land for which compensation has been determined.
predicates.shared_survey_land: Some land in the same survey number was acquired for the different projects being compared.
predicates.prior_comparable_award_higher: A prior determination set higher compensation for land found comparable to the land in the appeal.
predicates.significant_compensation_difference: The compensation determinations for the comparable lands differ substantially.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition compensation appeal concerns land comparable in location or survey identity to land with a higher prior award and the compensation difference is substantial, compensation is adjusted to a just and reasonable level.

issues.legal_issue: A prior judgment’s statement that it is not to be treated as a precedent may be confined to its exceptional treatment of post-notification sale deeds and need not prevent consideration of that judgment when assessing compensation for comparable land.
material_facts: The earlier judgment considered sale deeds executed after the acquisition notification because the parties agreed that the deeds were bona fide and could be considered.
That judgment described its decision as based on peculiar facts and not to be treated as a precedent.
The Court interpreted that qualification as applying to the exceptional consideration of post-notification sale deeds.
The land in the present appeals was found similarly situated to the land considered in the earlier judgment.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the earlier judgment’s qualification did not prevent it from considering that judgment in assessing just compensation for the similarly situated lands.
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed the qualification in Arawali Power Company Private Limited in context: it related to the exceptional reliance on post-Section 4 notification sale deeds, which ordinarily may not be considered, but which the parties had agreed were bona fide. The earlier judgment therefore remained relevant to the assessment of compensation for comparable land in the present case.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.prior_judgment_disclaimed_precedential_f: An earlier judgment stated that its decision was not to be treated as a precedent.
predicates.disclaimer_concerned_exceptional_sale_ev: The earlier judgment used that qualification in connection with its consideration of sale deeds made after the acquisition notification.
predicates.current_land_comparable_to_prior_land: The land in the current proceeding is found comparable to the land considered in the earlier judgment.

issues.definition: If a compensation appeal involves comparable land and an earlier judgment’s disclaimer concerned its exceptional consideration of sale evidence, that earlier judgment may be considered for the comparable land.

issues.legal_issue: A landowner whose appeal delay was condoned on the condition that no interest would be paid for the delay is not entitled to interest on the enhanced compensation for that delay.
material_facts: The High Court condoned delay in filing or refiling certain appeals on the condition that the landowners would not receive interest on any enhanced compensation for the period of delay.
The Supreme Court increased the compensation and otherwise allowed statutory benefits, but preserved the no-interest condition for those appeals.
issues.conclusion: The affected landowners were not entitled to interest on the enhanced compensation for the period of delay in filing or refiling their appeals before the High Court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court gave effect to the condition imposed when the High Court condoned the delay, while otherwise allowing statutory benefits under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. The judgment does not identify a specific statutory provision governing this no-interest condition.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.appeal_delay_condoned_on_no_interest_con: A court condoned delay in filing or refiling the appeal on the condition that interest would not be paid for the delay.
predicates.enhanced_compensation_awarded: The landowner received an increase in compensation in the proceeding.

issues.definition: When an enhanced-compensation appeal proceeds after delay has been condoned on a no-interest condition, interest is not payable for the period covered by that condition.
